input: Investigate apprenticeship programs in electrical work

gold.taskDescription: Research available apprenticeship programs in the electrical trade to evaluate options and determine next steps.

questions.title: Are you looking to start an apprenticeship yourself?
questions.description: Clarify whether this research is for personal enrollment or for another purpose such as hiring, advising someone else, or academic research.

questions.title: What country or region are you located in?
questions.description: Identify the geographic location to ensure the programs found are relevant and accessible.

questions.title: Do you have any prior electrical or trade experience?
questions.description: Understand the user's current skill or experience level to match programs that fit their background.

questions.title: Are you interested in residential, commercial, or industrial work?
questions.description: Determine which specialization within electrical work the user wants to pursue.

questions.title: Do you have a target timeline for when to start?
questions.description: Establish whether there is urgency or a specific intake window the user is aiming for.

questions.title: Is cost or financial aid a factor in your decision?
questions.description: Find out if program fees, wages during training, or scholarship availability need to be part of the investigation.

questions.title: Are union-based programs a preference or a requirement?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants to focus on union apprenticeships such as IBEW, non-union programs, or both.
